name: Phoenix
legend: One theory: Egypt's sacred Bennu bird, drawn as a heron, inspired the Greek phoenix.

name: Dragon
legend: In China, fossil bones were long sold as 'dragon bones' for medicine.

name: Griffin
legend: One theory suggests ancient fossil hunters mistook dinosaur skeletons for griffins.

name: Pegasus
legend: From Greek myth: the winged horse tamed by the hero Bellerophon.

name: Roc
legend: One theory: the giant elephant bird of Madagascar, now extinct.

name: Kitsune
legend: Kitsune are the red foxes of Japanese folklore; fox statues guard Inari shrines all over Japan.

name: Qilin
legend: When a giraffe was brought to the Chinese emperor in 1414, people called it a qilin.

name: Jackalope
legend: One theory: rabbits with a virus that grows horn-like bumps on their heads.

name: Unicorn
legend: Narwhal tusks were once sold in Europe as unicorn horns.

name: Yeti
legend: A 2017 DNA study found most supposed Yeti samples came from bears.

name: Bigfoot
legend: One theory: many sightings are black bears walking on their hind legs.

name: Black Tortoise
legend: From Chinese star lore: the guardian of the north, a tortoise wound with a snake.

name: Fenrir
legend: From Norse myth: a giant wolf the gods could only hold with a magic ribbon.

name: Nemean Lion
legend: Lions really lived in ancient Greece, until about 2,000 years ago.

name: Cerberus
legend: From Greek myth: the three-headed dog that guards the gate of the underworld.

name: Manticore
legend: One theory: Greek writers heard Persian tales of the tiger and turned it into a monster.

name: Chupacabra
legend: Many 'chupacabras' found in the US turned out to be coyotes with mange.

name: Loch Ness Monster
legend: A 2018 DNA survey of Loch Ness found lots of eel DNA and no reptile DNA.

name: Mongolian Death Worm
legend: Told by nomads of the Gobi Desert; explorer Roy Chapman Andrews wrote about it in 1926.

name: Kraken
legend: Likely inspired by sightings of giant squid.

name: Hydra
legend: The tiny freshwater hydra, which regrows when cut, was named after it.

name: Basilisk
legend: The real basilisk lizard, which runs across water, was named after it.

name: Sphinx
legend: Egypt's Great Sphinx, a lion with a human head, was carved about 4,500 years ago.

name: Baku
legend: In Japanese, the word for tapir is baku, and the dream-eater is often drawn like one.
